questions.q: How does the ploughing in Ndotsheni now go, at the demonstrator's direction?
choices: Straight up and down the hills as before
Round the hills, throwing up walls of earth, so the fields look different from the old days
Not at all, because of the drought
Only on the tops
questions.explain: The demonstrator still 'shakes his head' over how little food is in the soil.

questions.q: Why has the chief ordered a kraal to be built?
choices: To hold more cattle for wealth
So the cattle stay in one place and the dung can be easily collected and put back on the land
To keep the cattle safe from thieves
For the demonstrator to live in
questions.explain: It is 'a hard thing, because there will be nothing to eat in the kraal.'

questions.q: What new practice, unheard of in the valley, do the people adopt for the tree seed?
choices: Planting it at full moon
Boiling the wattle seed before planting
Soaking it in milk
Burning the ground first
questions.explain: Those who have worked for white farmers confirm it is right.

questions.q: How were these changes actually achieved?
choices: The people welcomed them eagerly
Through meetings marked by 'much silence, and much sullenness' — 'It was only the fear of the chief that made anything come out of these meetings'
By order of the magistrate
By paying the people
questions.explain: No one is more dissatisfied than those who must give up their fields to the dam.

questions.q: Why does Kuluse's brother eventually stop resisting the loss of his land?
choices: He is paid well for it
It is hard to refuse the umfundisi, through whom came the milk that saved his brother's child
The chief threatens him
He is given the best land instead
questions.explain: He is also consoled that Zuma and his brother will lose land next year too.

questions.q: What is 'the greatest wonder of all' brought into the valley?
choices: A tractor
A great machine that 'was fighting in the war', which pushes the earth into the wall of the dam
A water pump
An aeroplane
questions.explain: Even sullen Kuluse's brother 'breaks out into unwilling laughter' watching it.

questions.q: For whom does Letsitsi say he really works?
choices: For Jarvis, who pays him
'We work for Africa... not for this man or that man. Not for a white man or a black man, but for Africa'
For the chief
For himself
questions.explain: A white man taught him 'that we do not work for men, that we work for the land and the people.'

questions.q: What does Letsitsi argue that troubles Kumalo?
choices: That the church is useless
That even a restored Ndotsheni could not hold all the tribe if they returned — 'when the children grow up, there will again be too many'
That Jarvis should be repaid in money
That farming cannot be taught
questions.explain: Kumalo sighs, 'You are too clever for me.'

questions.q: What does Letsitsi say about what the good white man does for the valley?
choices: That it is a pure gift
That it is 'only a repayment' — because the white man gave them so little land and took them away to work
That it is charity to be grateful for forever
That it is not enough to matter
questions.explain: Kumalo says he does not like this talk, and reminds Letsitsi to 'hate no man, and desire power over no man.'

questions.q: What warning does Kumalo give the young demonstrator?
choices: To leave the valley
'Hate no man, and desire power over no man. For I have a friend who taught me that power corrupts.'
To obey the chief in all things
To ask Jarvis for more money
questions.explain: 'For there is enough hating in our land already.'
